28551.description:
SAFETY AND TRAINING COORDINATOR - LAE


Chemcare Group is seeking a motivated and experienced Safety and Training Coordinator to be based at our Head Office in Lae. Reporting to the Group Security Manager, the incumbent will play a key role in promoting a strong safety culture while, coordinating employee training and development programs across the organization.


 


Key Responsibilities include:




Identify workplace training needs in consultation with departmental managers and supervisors.


Develop, coordinate, and maintain training schedules and competency matrices.


Conduct in-house safety inductions, training, toolbox talks, and workplace awareness sessions.


Coordinate specialized safety training with external training providers and statutory authorities.


Develop and maintain safety training modules, SOPs, and emergency evacuation plans.


Assess training effectiveness and maintain accurate safety training records in the Pronto database.


Plan and implement Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) programs and initiatives.


Investigate workplace incidents and injuries, identify causes, and recommend corrective actions.


Monitor workplace activities, repairs, and installations to ensure employee safety and regulatory compliance.


Prepare safety reports and perform other safety-related duties as directed by senior management.




 


Qualification and Experience




Diploma or certificate in Safety, Training or HSE Coordination role.


Good knowledge and understanding of workplace safety practices and risk managements


Past experience (5years or more) in conducting training and facilitating presentations


Strong organization, written and verbal skills plus reporting skills


Computer literate


Knowledge of PNG Employment and Workplace regulations is an advantage




 


To apply, send your  application as
 
One PDF File
 including
 
cover letter, CV, and copies of relevant documents
 to
:


 


The Group Human Resource Manager 


Chemcare Group Ltd, P.O. Box 349, Lae, 411, Morobe Province


E-mail address: 
[email protected]


 


Electronic applications are encouraged. 


 


Applications close 2
nd
 October 202
6


 


 








Apply

Position Title: Web Developer


Location: Head Office – Port Moresby
Department: Application Support


Division: Daltron


 


Overview


We are seeking a talented and motivated 
Web Developer
 
/ Applications Support Specialist
 to join our Applications Support team. The Web Developer / Application Support Specialist plays a dual role in Daltron’s ICT operations: developing and maintaining web applications while ensuring reliable support for both internal teams and external customers. Internally, the role supports staff by maintaining business-critical systems, streamlining workflows, and enabling operational efficiency. Externally, the role provides technical assistance to clients, ensuring smooth application performance, timely issue resolution, and delivery of enhancements that meet customer requirements. This position is key to sustaining Daltron’s reputation for dependable ICT solutions and customer-focused service.


Key Responsibilities




Design, develop and maintain responsive web applications and portals.


Implement clean, efficient and secure code following industry best practices.


Collaborate with cross-function teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions.


Provide first and second level support for business applications.


Troubleshoot, diagnose and resolve application issues in a timely manner.


Monitor system performance and ensure high availability of applications.


Coordinate with vendors and third-party providers when required.


Develop API and integration between applications and enterprise systems.


Support ERP, CRM and other business platforms and customization and reporting.


Participate in upgrades, migration and testing activities.


Maintain technical documentation, user guides and support materials.


Provide training and guidance to end users on application functionality.




 


Qualifications, Skills & Experience




Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology or related filed.


Proven experience in web development (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP or similar frameworks).


Knowledge of database management (SQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL).


Experience with ERP systems, APIS, and application integration is an advantage.


Frappe/Bench framework knowledge is a strong advantage.


Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure.


Excellent communication and interpersonal skills for user support and collaboration.




 


Preferred Attributes




Familiarity with ICT infrastructure and enterprise applications.


Ability to balance development tasks with operational support.


Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering quality solutions.


Team oriented mindset with proactive approach to continuous improvement.




 


 


How to Apply:


If you're excited to join a dynamic team and make a real impact, we'd love to hear from you!


Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your experience and why you'd be a great fit for this role to 
[email protected]
 or by clicking 
Apply 
below. 


Application closes by COB 
Friday, 02 October 2026

28509.description:
Child Protection Program Officer 


Position Description


 










Reporting to:






ANCP Provincial Coordinator






Work location:






Buka or Wewak










Department:






Program Operations

No










Grade






4

No










 


Here you’ll make a difference


Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods. The ANCP-funded Child Protection Project is a four-year project implemented from August 2025 to July 2029 in the provinces of East Sepik and the Autonomous Region of Bougainville.


 


Here your skills will be valued


Role Purpose


Reporting to the Provincial Coordinators, the Child Protection Program Officers in East Sepik and Autonomous Region of Bougainville will support the delivery of the ANCP-funded Child Protection programming in each province by engaging with community’ facilitators, community leaders, schools, caregivers, children, government agencies, and other stakeholders to implement project activities. The role will provide mentoring to community facilitators and work with care givers, teachers, community leaders, and stakeholders to implement project activities and ensure effective delivery of the project.


 


Key Areas of Accountability


Project Implementation




Ensure understanding of project design, objectives, outputs and activities; and develop workplans in line with the project’s implementation plan.


Implement and maintain strong and positive community engagement activities.


Work with communities to identify, select, and train Community Volunteers (Facilitators); and provide regular oversight, mentoring and coaching throughout the project.


Participate in all trainings relevant to the project and other trainings as needed/ requested.


Engage regularly with government agencies as needed and requested; assist in implementing project advocacy and capacity-building activities at provincial headquarters.


Support implementation of child participation and child-led advocacy activities.


Assist in the utilization of all project management tools, such as Project Management Method (PMM) and other mandatory tools.


Ensure activities are planned and implemented in line with the budget and available resources, and in line with procurement and financial policies and procedures.


Work with the Monitoring, Evaluation, Assessment, and Learning (MEAL) team to ensure data collection tools are used correctly and accurately to track progress on project indicators and targets. Participate in all learning activities.


Complete all activity and other reports as needed and requested.


Work with the MEAL team to ensure community feedback mechanisms are implemented.


Assist in identifying project risks and in applying mitigation strategies.


Any other relevant responsibility as assigned by the supervisor.




 


Other / General




Ensure adherence to all Save the Children policies and procedures.


Provide regular reports and updates as needed; and participate in performance reviews.


Any other tasks as needed and requested.




 


Child protection and safeguarding requirements




Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.


Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s 
Child Safeguarding Policy
, 
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.


Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behaviour towards children in private and professional life.


Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.


Maintain a safe and positive relationship at all times when working with children and young people.


Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.




 


Health, safety, security and risk management 
 




Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training.


Act safely at all times.


Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.


Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.


Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.




 


All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.


At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.


 


Person Specification


It takes all types of people to do the challenging work we do. Here are some of the specific skills and experiences you’ll bring in this role:


 


Qualifications/Accreditations




Relevant tertiary qualification in Social Work, Community Development, Education, Health or related field; or significant related field experience.


Minimum three (3) years’ experience implementing programs in child protection/ community development or related field.


Experience working with NGOs is an added advantage.


Strong facilitation, communication and community engagement skills and experience.


Experience working with government, stakeholders, and communities.


Excellent reporting, English writing, and documentation skills.


Strong activity planning, budget management, and delivery skills.


Knowledge of child protection principles and safeguarding standards.


Local knowledge and/or experience in either of the project provinces, East Sepik and Bougainville; knowledge of a key local languages in the province is an added advantage.


Knowledge of gender equality and diversity principles is an added advantage.


Must be a team player and can maintain reputation of self and organization.


Willing to travel to and work in remote areas with challenging infrastructure.




 


Additional Information 




Any offer of employment at Save the Children Australia will be subject to a satisfactory National Police Record Check and a Working with Children Check


Employees must sign on to Save the Children Australia’s Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct


Ongoing performance and employment will be measured against KPIs, values and demonstrated behaviours outlined above


Save the Children Australia is an Equal Opportunity Employer




 










 






 






 






 










Working with Children Check:






Required






Travel:






Frequent within the province is expected

Field Manager 
Position Description










Reporting to:






Program Operations Director






Work location:






Simbu  / ENB










Department:






Program Operations






Budget holder:






Yes, as delegated under the IDD










Grade






6






Direct reports:






Support & Program Leads in the Field Office










 


Here you’ll make a difference


Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children implements programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance, and livelihoods in four (4) provinces across PNG and the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (AROB).  In four of these areas, Field Managers provide leadership and oversight to the programming and teams in that area.


 


Here your skills will be valued - Role Purpose


 


Reporting to the Program Operations Director, Field Managers are responsible for effectively leading and overseeing program delivery and support functions (finance, supply chain, admin) in their respective locations / provinces. The FM is responsible for ensuring quality program delivery that is on time and within budget in their respective locations, as well as overseeing effective support functions. FMs report directly to the Program Operations Director and generally provide direct line management of program and support leads in their site.  FMs are also responsible for overseeing the implementation of programs / projects in their provinces which do not have a designated lead in that province. The FM will serve as a member of Save the Children in PNG’s Extended Management Team (ESMT) and will play am important humanitarian leadership role in the even of any humanitarian emergency or situation.


 


Key Areas of Accountability


 


Project Implementation and MEAL  




In collaboration with provincial and program leads, ensure that program staff are supported and guided to deliver on project goals, objectives, expected results and donor requirements.


Ensure that all program staff are delivering activities using standardized tools and processes (with exceptions for specific donor requirements).


Host and coordinate senior management and/or technical support visits as feasible, ensuring that such visits are used as opportunities to strengthen processes and quality programming.


Guide and support project/program leads and teams to fully understand their project budgets, and to analyse expenses, classifications, and variances each month, with actions taken as needed.


Work with the MEAL team leadership to ensure that MEAL staff are fulfilling their functions effectively, helping to monitor quality programming, data collection and learning, and ensuring that beneficiary feedback mechanisms are fully functional and used.


Help coordinator program reflection and learning activities in collaboration with MEAL and technical teams, with learning shared across the country office.


Serve as a provincial lead for projects that are implemented but do not have a lead in that province.




 


 


Oversight of Support Functions




Oversight of and support to all financial functions in that office, in consultation with the national finance team, ensuring they adhere to Save the Children and donor-specific financial policies and procedures. Ensure all staff in the field office comply with policies at all times.


Oversight of all supply chain and admin functions, including procurement, asset and warehouse management, and fleet management, in line with Save the Children policies and procedures.


In collaboration with the P&C team, ensure that all HR policies and procedures are followed, and that staff performance (KPI) plans and reviews are completed according to schedule.


Serve as a security and risk management focal point for the field office, ensuring full adherence to safety and security procedures, and liaising regularly with the security team at national level.




 


Leadership:




Foster a strong understanding and daily practice of Save the Children’s values, country strategy and quality standards within the provincial team, also serving as a role model.


Serve as a member of Save the Children in PNG’s Extended Management Team (ESMT).


Foster a strong culture of collaboration between the program, MEAL, and support functions, and provide opportunities for all functions to contribute to quality program delivery


Seek opportunities to advance Save the Children’s Country Strategy in the province where possible, and in consultation with the program quality / new business development team. Assist with the development of new proposals as needed and requested.


Ensure adherence to policies and procedures; lead in security and risk management.




 


External Relations; Stakeholder Management




Build strong relationships with key sub-national stakeholders, including provincial and district government, relevant CSOs and FBOs, academic institutions and the private sector.


Foster a culture of external collaboration among the provincial team and encourage staff to build relationships with key stakeholders at all levels.


Work with the provincial teams to strengthen and maintain positive, mutually respectful relationships with partners and stakeholders working directly with SC’s programs.




 


General




Ensure full compliance (self and team) with Save the Children’s/ donor policies and procedures.


Hold regular team meetings and 1-to-1 meetings with direct reports, which are documented.


Any other tasks as needed and requested.




 


Child protection and safeguarding requirements




Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.


Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s 
Child Safeguarding Policy
, 
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.


Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behaviour towards children in private and professional life.


Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being part of Save the Children’s family.


Maintain a safe and positive relationship when working with children and young people.


Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.

Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training.


Act safely at all times.


Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.


Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.


Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.

Qualifications/Accreditations

A minimum of seven (7) years’ work experience – preferably in an NGO environment, and with at least two years managing a field office or sub-office and team.




 


Skills, abilities and experience




Strong project management skills and demonstrated experience in managing complex projects and/or multiple projects at the same time


Experience implementing or overseeing support systems (finance, HR, admin, procurement), ensuring adherence to procedures and strong control systems in a remote context.

The ability to effectively coordinate resources and drive outcomes quickly.


Solid computer skills: word, excel, powerpoint, etc.


Good communication skills both in English and Tok-Pisin; excellent writing / documentation skills.


A willingness to travel to regional/project locations within PNG.


Able to work harmoniously in cross cultural environments, resolve conflicts and build teams.

Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high-quality Flour, Stock Feed, Rice, Snacks, and Bakery products throughout the country. Well-known products and brands include Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Flame Oil & Sugar, Flame Rice, Bilas Bread, Skel Rice, Twisties snacks, Arthur’s Pie, and the Meadow Lea range.


At GFI, we care about making everyday food better for everyone.


Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative local food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.


We currently have an immediate vacancy for a
 Boiler Technician
 who will be responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of the site’s boiler systems and associated utilities. This role ensures continuous steam supply to production lines, performs routine maintenance, and supports the overall reliability of utilities infrastructure in our operations in
 Lae
. The objective of this position is to monitor all boiler operators and attend to any boiler maintenance problem or break down including boiler water quality testings as well (including some statistical analysis). The ideal candidate must be able to operate the RO system proficiently and continuously monitor water quality.


 


Your
 
responsibilities
 
will include
:




Boiler Operation & Monitoring






Operate, monitor, and control boiler systems to ensure consistent steam supply for production.


Conduct routine checks on pressure, temperature, water levels, fuel supply, and safety devices.


Record operational data in logbooks and digital systems.




 




Maintenance & Repairs






Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on boilers, feed pumps, valves, burners, and water treatment systems.


Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and control issues affecting boiler performance.


Assist in major shutdowns, overhauls, and inspections.


 






Safety & Compliance






Ensure all boiler operations comply with PNG safety regulations and internal GFI policies.


Maintain and test safety valves, alarms, gauges, and emergency shutdown systems.


Support workplace safety initiatives, including hazard identification and risk assessments.




 




Water Treatment & Quality Control






Monitor and maintain boiler water quality, including chemical dosing and blowdown procedures.


Conduct water tests to prevent scaling, corrosion, and carryover.




 




Documentation & Reporting






Maintain accurate maintenance records, daily logs, and incident reports.


Report abnormalities, breakdowns, and potential risks to the Utilities Supervisor.




 




Cross‑Functional Support






Assist with other utilities systems such as air compressors, generators, and refrigeration units when required.


Support production teams during peak operations or emergencies.




 


To be considered for the role, you will need to have
:




Trade Certificate or Qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Fitting & Machining, or related field.


PNG Boiler Operator Certification (Class 1 or Class 2).


Minimum 3 years’ experience operating Industrial Boilers (fire‑tube or water‑tube).


Strong understanding of boiler safety standards and water treatment processes.




Work Environment




Industrial manufacturing setting with exposure to heat, steam, noise, and rotating machinery.


Requires use of PPE and adherence to GFI safety protocols at all times

28715.description:

The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-governmental organisation committed to working with communities, government, and other partners to manage wildlife and wild places for biodiversity and human well-being.

Document impacts of livelihood interventions, including but not restricted to yields, sales and profits.

Qualifications and Experience




Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Marine Resource Management, Environmental Science, Development Studies, Fisheries, or related discipline) is preferred. However, candidates with substantial relevant experience in livelihoods development projects, particularly in marine and coastal settings, will be given equal consideration.


At least two years’ full-time professional experience in implementing marine and coastal-focused livelihood projects with the private sector and non-governmental organization (NGO) or a government agency or equivalent


Strong understanding of and experience conducting financial and business management training for communities


Good interpersonal skills and experience in liaising with a range of stakeholders, including traditional landowners, local and state government, special interest groups and individuals regarding natural resource management issues.




 


Critical Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities




Experience in community engagement, facilitation, and participatory planning.


Experience working with communities, and customary institutions.


Strong facilitation and conflict-sensitive communication skills.

Good analytical and problem-solving skills


Good knowledge of written and spoken English and Tok Pisin


Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence

Excellent organisational and leadership skills


Excellent communication skills


Ability to work with less supervision and under pressure

Monier Limited the single largest producer, supplier and distributor or construction materials and building products in PNG is seeking to recruit suitably qualified and highly motivated individual for the following positions:


1 X Heavy Equipment Fitter


The Heavy Equipment Fitter is responsible for safely and efficiently maintaining, diagnosing, repairing and inspecting heavy equipment machinery to ensure maximum fleet availability and reliability. The role supports operational performance through quality workmanship, compliance with maintenance processes, teamwork, continuous improvement and adherence to Monier safety standards and procedures.


Duties Include:




Perform scheduled servicing, preventative maintenance and component replacements on heavy mobile equipment.


Diagnose mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic and powertrain faults using OEM diagnostic tools and equipment.


Conduct engine, transmission, differential, brake and hydraulic system repairs.


Carry out major component rebuilds and machine overhauls.

28539.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Purpose
The Supervisor Reliability will lead a team to assess and improve asset reliability through standard methodologies, root cause analyses, data analytics, operations collaboration, defect elimination and analysis of asset strategy effectiveness to ensure business objectives are met.


Essential Duties




Lead and mentor a reliability team to assess asset performance, identify improvement opportunities, and optimise operational effectiveness. 


Evaluate existing asset management strategies, identify performance gaps, and implement initiatives to improve asset reliability and availability. 


Monitor mechanical asset compliance with relevant legislation, standards, and company requirements, providing recommendations to address identified risks and gaps. 


Assess, prioritise, and champion reliability improvement initiatives based on business objectives, risk profiles, and potential operational impact. 


Develop and execute reliability programs for fixed plant and mobile equipment, leveraging industry best practices and innovative maintenance methodologies. 


Facilitate site reliability reviews and audits to evaluate asset management effectiveness and drive continuous improvement across operations. 


Collaborate closely with operations, maintenance, and technical stakeholders to align asset strategies and ensure sustainable reliability outcomes. 


Lead and oversee root cause failure analyses (RCFA) for fixed plant and mobile equipment, ensuring effective corrective and preventive actions are implemented. 


Monitor and report on asset reliability KPIs, providing actionable insights and regular performance updates to site and corporate leadership teams. 


Develop and deliver training and capability development programs that promote reliability-centred maintenance principles and best practices. 


Utilise data analytics and reliability engineering tools to evaluate equipment performance, identify trends, and drive data-informed maintenance and asset management decisions. 


Foster a culture of continuous improvement, safety, and operational excellence through proactive reliability and asset management leadership.




Training & Experience




Practical experience in asset reliability, data analysis, and performance reporting is essential.


Formal education in engineering or training in reliability concepts and tools is essential.


Previous responsibility for creating and optimizing asset strategies is beneficial.


Competency in reliability systems and programs, defect elimination, root cause analysis, and asset strategy optimization.


Proficiency in data analytics.


Foundational knowledge and skills in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.




Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.


At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​


Learn more about our purpose and values: About Newmont​
Hear from our people: Life at Newmont​


Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: 
[email protected]
.

Location: Port Moresby

We have an immediate requirement for a Mechanical Technician to join our Planned Maintenance Team in Port Moresby, reporting to the Planned Maintenance Team Leader.


 


Key Responsibilities


 




Equipment Maintenance:
 Perform routine preventive and corrective maintenance on plant machinery including conveyors, fillers, cappers, labelers, pumps, motors, and gearboxes.


Fault Diagnostics:
 Diagnose mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic breakdowns rapidly to minimize production downtime on high-speed lines.


Continuous Improvement:

Safety and Compliance:

Documentation:
 Maintain equipment histories, service schedules, work logs, and critical spare parts inventory levels.


Record Keeping:
 Log all maintenance activities, parts used, and equipment conditions in a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).




 


 


Qualifications & Requirements


 




Education:
 A recognized mechanical trade qualification, or a related technical field.


Experience:
 2 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience working with automated, rotating, or high-speed manufacturing equipment—ideally within the food and beverage sector.


Technical Skills:
 Strong mechanical aptitude, proficiency in reading blueprints and schematics, and familiarity with hydraulic, pneumatic, and electrical systems.


Soft Skills:
 Good problem-solving abilities, teamwork, and communication skills to work alongside engineers and production staff.

28472.description:
About Newmont


 


At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.


 


About Lihir


 


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
 










Purpose






 


Responsible for providing civil and structural engineering design and modifications within the process plant and associated mine site infrastructure that shall meet company specifications, comply with operational requirements, agreements and relevant standards.










Essential Duties






 




Provide civil and structural engineering designs and calculations to relevant design codes and standards.


Review and investigate proposed structural modifications within the process plant and mine site infrastructure and provide engineering guidance.


Conduct site inspections and prepare conceptual structural design options for presentations to clients and stakeholders.


Prepare for review detailed drawings suitable for construction.


Liaise with inter-departmental clients, stakeholders and external consultants if necessary for design parameters and project requirements.


Identify and evaluate potential risks related to structural designs and construction methodologies, implementing robust mitigation strategies to enhance safety and project viability.


Provide technical support during the construction and installation phases, ensuring structures are built according to the design specifications.












Training & Experience






 




Bachelor’s Degree qualification in Civil Engineering, 3-5 years of structural engineering experience in a mining or heavy industry environment.


Demonstrated competence in the application of Australian Standards 


Strong technical capability in steel structures and structural concrete.


Strong attention to detail and documentation capability.


Experience in the use Space Gass Software.
Strong capability to perform relevant engineering calculations to support designs.


Able to read, understand and prepare engineering drawings.


Capability to review engineering drawings and red-line in consultation with the design team to ensure accurate design and construction drawings.


Excellent planning and organizational skills.


Excellent communication skills and ability to work with minimal supervision


Good computer literacy and understanding of Microsoft software suite


Understanding of safety compliance and regulations


Registered with IEPNG


Valid Class 6 Driving License 












Working Conditions






 


This is a FIFO opportunity based at Newmont's Lihir operation in Papua New Guinea, working a 21 days on / 21 days off roster. The role combines office-based engineering design with field inspections, stakeholder engagement and construction support within a large-scale gold processing and mining environment.










At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.


We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.

28471.description:
As an experienced Auto Electrical Technician supporting the Truckshop team, you will provide technical auto sparkie skills, leadership, and mentoring in the maintenance, diagnosis, and repair of electrical and electronic systems across Newmont's mobile fleet, with a primary focus on CAT 785D, 777F, and 773D haul trucks.


Your role is critical in improving equipment reliability, availability, and maintenance quality while developing the capability of your core worker and apprentices. You will act as the technical authority for auto electrical systems, providing hands-on support, coaching, and guidance to ensure maintenance activities are completed safely and to OEM standards.


Working in a demanding mining environment, you will drive continuous improvement initiatives, strengthen workforce capability, and contribute directly to Newmont's operational excellence objectives.


---


Key Responsibilities


Duties:


-- Provide technical support for auto electrical systems across the mobile fleet.


-- Lead complex fault-finding and diagnostic activities on haul trucks and ancillary equipment.


-- Support troubleshooting and repair of:


o Wiring harnesses


o Electronic Control Modules (ECMs)


o Sensors and switches


o Starting and charging systems


o Lighting systems


o Telematics and fleet management systems


o Product Link Elite (PLE)


o Health Monitoring Systems (HIMS)


o Collision avoidance systems


o Camera systems


o Communication equipment


-- Ensure repairs and maintenance activities are completed to OEM and Newmont standards.


-- Guide and oversee component replacements, planned maintenance, and breakdown repairs.


-- Monitor equipment performance and identify emerging reliability risks.


-- Improve maintenance practices through technical feedback and practical solutions.


-- Coach, mentor, and develop Auto Electricians, Technicians, and Apprentices.


-- Promote knowledge transfer and sustainable workforce development.


-- Champion Newmont's Safety Values and Critical Control Management standards.


-- Ensure compliance with all site safety procedures, isolation processes, and statutory requirements.


-- Lead by example in hazard identification, risk management, and incident prevention.


-- Stop unsafe work and promote a strong safety culture.


-- Ensure work activities comply with environmental and regulatory requirements.


---


-- Delivering safe and quality auto electrical maintenance outcomes.


-- Reducing repeat electrical failures and downtime.


-- Ensuring compliance with Newmont maintenance and safety standards.


---


Qualifications


Essential


-- Recognised NATTB Trade Qualification in Automotive Electrical Technology or equivalent.


-- Current and valid driver's licence (PNG Class or ability to obtain).


-- Strong understanding of heavy mobile equipment electrical systems.


-- Demonstrated capability in advanced electrical diagnostics and fault-finding.


-- Extensive experience maintaining, diagnosing, and repairing heavy mining equipment electrical systems.


-- Significant experience working on CAT 785D, 777F, and 773D haul trucks or equivalent mining equipment.

28469.description:
About Newmont


At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.


 


About Lihir


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


 


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Your impact


Reporting to the Supervisor - Mechanical - Shovel Pad, you will be responsible for safely carrying out inspection, fault finding, maintenance, repair, and testing activities on a range of heavy mining equipment.


Your primary focus will be supporting shovel and drill assets while ensuring all work is completed in accordance with safety, maintenance, and operational standards.


---


As part of the team you will


-- Perform inspection, diagnosis, troubleshooting, repair and testing of mobile mining equipment electrical systems.


-- Maintain and repair heavy mining equipment to required operational and safety standards.


-- Complete accurate maintenance documentation and service records.


-- Contribute to equipment reliability and fleet availability targets.


-- Identify and report opportunities for cost reduction and waste minimisation.


-- Demonstrate a strong commitment to Health, Safety and Environmental standards.


-- Work collaboratively within a diverse and inclusive team environment.


---


Prerequisites for the role


-- Trade Certificate in Auto Electrical Technology or equivalent qualification.


-- Minimum 3 to 5 years' experience in heavy industry, preferably within mining.


-- Proven experience maintaining and troubleshooting mobile fleet equipment.


-- Strong commitment to safety and safe work practices.


-- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.


-- Strong problem-solving and fault-finding capability.


-- High attention to detail and effective time management skills.


-- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.


-- Current PNG Class 6 Driver's Licence.


Desirable Experience


Experience working on the following equipment will be highly regarded:


-- Hitachi EX2600 Excavators


-- O&K RH200 Hydraulic Excavators


-- Caterpillar 6020 & 6060 Mining Shovels


-- Epiroc D65 Drills


-- Epiroc/Atlas Copco PV231 & PV271 Pit Viper Blast Hole Drills


 


 


Your Work Environment


This role is offered on a 28:14 Day / Night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG from our approved POH.


Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suite and air-conditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.


Why Join Newmont


At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.


 


We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you

Remote Unique Hotel | Papua New Guinea


An exceptional opportunity to lead a distinctive upmarket hotel in one of Papua New Guinea's remote and beautiful locations. 


We are seeking an experienced, hands-on 
Hotel Manager 
to take responsibility for the day-to-day operation of a small, high-quality hotel with fewer than 60 rooms. Several positions are available.


This is an opportunity for an accomplished hospitality professional who enjoys working in a remote environment, takes pride in exceptional guest service, and is capable of leading a team while maintaining high operational standards.


The Role


Reporting to the general manager, the Hotel Manager will have overall responsibility for the hotel's operations, guest experience, staff performance and commercial results. The successful candidate will be comfortable being highly visible and hands-on. In a small hotel, the manager is expected to lead from the front, solve problems quickly and ensure that every guest receives a consistently high standard of service.


Key Responsibilities


 Oversee the daily operation of the hotel, including rooms, food and beverage, guest services, housekeeping and maintenance.


 Lead, motivate and develop the hotel team, creating a professional and positive working environment.


 Maintain consistently high standards of guest service and presentation.


 Manage to meet the targets of budget, costs, purchasing and operational performance.


 Monitor occupancy, revenue and other key performance indicators.


 Manage stock levels and purchasing in an environment where supplies may require careful planning and transportation.


 Ensure rooms, public areas, facilities and grounds are maintained to a high standard.


 Work closely with local staff and communities and encourage staff development.


 Handle guest requests, complaints and unexpected operational issues professionally.


 Ensure appropriate health, safety, security and operating procedures are followed.


 Plan ahead for the particular logistical challenges of operating a hotel in a remote location.


 Represent the hotel professionally with guests, suppliers, business partners and the local community.


 Work closely with the management team to identify opportunities to improve the hotel's performance and guest experience.


About You


We are looking for a capable and experienced hospitality professional who combines
 strong management skills with a practical, hands-on approach and basic maintenance.


You will ideally have:


 Previous experience managing a hotel, resort, lodge or comparable hospitality operation.


 Proven leadership and staff-management experience.


 Strong understanding of hotel operations and financial management.


 Excellent guest-service and communication skills.


 The ability to work calmly and effectively under pressure.


 Strong organisational and problem-solving skills.


 A genuine commitment to maintaining high standards.


 The flexibility and resilience required to live and work in a remote location.


 Experience in Papua New Guinea, the Pacific, remote resorts or similar environments would be highly regarded. Most importantly, you will be someone who takes 
ownership, leads by example, gets things done and operate independently.


Working in a Remote Location


This position will suit someone who enjoys the lifestyle and challenges of working away from a major city. The successful applicant should be comfortable with the realities of remote hotel operations, including logistical constraints, limited access to suppliers and services, and the need to plan well ahead. At the same time, the position offers the opportunity to live and work in a unique part of Papua New Guinea and to be part of a distinctive hospitality operation.


What We Offer


 An opportunity to lead a unique upmarket hotel in Papua New Guinea.


 A senior management position with significant responsibility and autonomy as per company policies.


 Competitive salary and benefits, commensurate with experience.


 Accommodation and other employment benefits appropriate to a remote location.


 The opportunity to make a genuine difference to the hotel's performance and guest experience.


 A rewarding lifestyle in a unique and remote environment.


How to Apply


Please submit your 
CV/resume and a covering letter
 outlining your relevant hotel management experience, your leadership approach, and why you are interested in working in a remote location in Papua New Guinea.

[email protected]

28328.description:
Summary






The Heavy Equipment Electrician is responsible for electrical troubleshooting, repairs, and preventive maintenance on heavy machinery such as excavators, trucks, generators, and loaders. The role covers PMS checks, diagnostics, and replacement of electrical components while ensuring all work is done safely and on schedule. The electrician also supports mechanics during servicing and assists with general workshop tasks when required. The position reports to the Workshop Supervisor or Fleet Maintenance Manager.


Key Responsibilities


 


- Inspect, diagnose, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain electrical and electronic systems on heavy equipment.


- Perform electrical fault finding using diagnostic tools, wiring diagrams, schematics, and manufacturer manuals.


- Repair and replace wiring harnesses, batteries, alternators, starters, sensors, switches, relays, lighting systems, and other electrical components.


- Diagnose faults in electronic control systems, including engine and equipment monitoring systems.


- Conduct preventive maintenance and scheduled inspections to ensure equipment reliability and safety.


- Demonstrate sound knowledge of hydraulic systems to assist in diagnosing and identifying equipment faults.


- Apply strong understanding of mechanical systems, including components and their operation.


- Possess working knowledge of diesel engines and transmission systems to support effective troubleshooting and repairs.


- Work closely with mechanical technicians and other maintenance personnel to resolve complex equipment issues.


- Read and interpret electrical, hydraulic, and mechanical schematics and technical manuals.


- Ensure all repairs and maintenance activities comply with company procedures, safety standards, and manufacturer specifications.


- Maintain accurate records of inspections, repairs, parts used, and maintenance activities.


- Identify potential equipment failures and recommend corrective actions.


- Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area.


Key Competencies


 


- Electrical troubleshooting and fault diagnosis


- Heavy equipment maintenance and repair


- Hydraulic system knowledge


- Mechanical system knowledge


- Engine and transmission knowledge


- Diagnostic equipment operation


- Technical documentation interpretation


- Problem-solving and attention to detail


- Teamwork and communication


- Safety awareness and compliance


 


Job Requirements






Qualifications and Requirements


 


- Trade qualification or technical certification in Automotive Electrical, Heavy Equipment Electrical, or a related field.


- Proven experience as a Heavy Equipment Electrician, preferably working with mining, construction, or industrial equipment.


- Strong knowledge of heavy equipment electrical and electronic systems.


- Sound knowledge of hydraulic systems and their basic operation and troubleshooting principles.


- Sound knowledge of mechanical systems and components.


- Good working knowledge of diesel engines and transmission systems.


- Ability to diagnose electrical and electronic faults using appropriate diagnostic equipment.


- Ability to read and interpret electrical wiring diagrams, schematics, and technical documentation.


- Experience working with heavy machinery such as excavators, bulldozers, loaders, dump trucks, graders, and other earthmoving equipment is preferred.


- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.


- Ability to work independently and as part of a maintenance team.


- Good communication and reporting skills.


- Commitment to workplace health, safety, and environmental standards.

Summary






The role is responsible for overseeing all areas managed by Security Compliance and Safety Officers, including fleet security, corporate security, and OSH/risk management. This position ensures that all security and safety operations are compliant with relevant standards, effectively managing risks and maintaining high standards of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH). The individual will coordinate activities, provide guidance, and ensure consistent implementation of safety protocols across the organization. Depending on the organizational needs, the focus on specific areas may vary, requiring flexibility and adaptability.


Duties and Responsibilities








Leadership and Supervision:




Supervise and provide direction to Security Compliance and Safety Officers.


Coordinate and oversee the daily activities of security and safety personnel.


Ensure consistency in the implementation of security and safety protocols across all departments.


Prioritize and shift focus between fleet security, corporate security, and OSH/risk management based on current organizational requirements.






Compliance:




Oversee the compliance of all security and safety operations with relevant standards and regulations.


Conduct regular compliance audits and inspections across various departments.


Ensure up-to-date maintenance of compliance documentation and policies.






Risk Management and OSH:




Supervise the development and implementation of OSH policies and procedures.


Conduct comprehensive risk assessments and hazard analyses across all operational areas.


Oversee investigations of incidents and accidents, ensuring corrective actions are implemented.


Ensure all project sites and company premises are set up and maintained within OSH standards.


Supervise the works to ensure compliance with OSH standards and report immediately to the manager if any site or premise does not meet the required standards.






Training and Development:




Develop and coordinate comprehensive training programs for security and safety officers.


Organize regular drills and emergency response training sessions.


Provide ongoing professional development opportunities for the team.






Reporting and Documentation:




Maintain accurate records of security incidents, safety inspections, risk assessments, and compliance activities.


Prepare and present detailed reports on security and safety performance to senior management.


Ensure all documentation is compliant with legal and regulatory requirements.






Coordination and Communication:




Act as the primary point of contact between security and safety officers and senior management.


Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between different departments and teams.


Coordinate with external security agencies and law enforcement as necessary.








Job Requirements








Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Occupational Safety, Risk Management, or a related field.


Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or similar certification preferred.


Minimum of 7 years of experience in security and safety management, with at least 3 years in a supervisory role.


Strong knowledge of relevant safety and security standards and regulations.


Experience in policing, security, or military preferred.


Martial arts skills preferred.


Valid driver's license and the ability to drive.


Strong leadership, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.


Ability to effectively manage and coordinate multiple projects and teams.


Flexibility to adapt and prioritize assignments in different areas as organizational needs change.




This role may require working in shifts, including nights and weekends. The supervisor may need to respond to emergencies outside of regular working hours. The working environment can be remote and may involve high-risk areas. The individual must be prepared to travel to various project sites and company premises as required to ensure compliance with OSH standards.


Required to travel to areas where needed.

Summary






The Class 7 (Heavy Equipment) Operator will operate and maintain multiple types of heavy equipment, including backhoes, rollers, loaders, excavators, and more. They will perform various tasks related to excavation, construction, and earthmoving operations while ensuring the safe and efficient operation of the equipment.


Duties and Responsibilities








Operate and control heavy equipment, such as boom crane, backhoes, rollers, loaders, excavators, and other machinery, following safety guidelines and best practices.


Perform routine pre-start inspections and maintenance checks on equipment to ensure proper functionality.


Operate equipment to excavate, grade, level, and move earth, rocks, debris, or other materials as required for construction or maintenance projects.


Ensure accurate positioning and maneuvering of heavy equipment to achieve project goals and specifications.


Comply with project plans, drawings, and instructions to carry out excavation and earthmoving activities.


Monitor and maintain adequate fuel and lubricant levels in equipment, refilling as necessary.


Operate heavy equipment safely and efficiently, adhering to all safety regulations and protocols.


Report any equipment malfunctions, breakdowns, or incidents to supervisors or maintenance staff.


Follow proper storage and maintenance procedures for heavy equipment during non-operational periods.


Collaborate with project teams, supervisors, and other operators to ensure smooth operations and timely project completion.


Maintain accurate records of equipment usage, maintenance activities, and production outputs.


Adhere to company policies, procedures, and safety standards at all times.


Perform any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.




Job Requirements








Valid driver's license with appropriate endorsements to operate heavy equipment.


Proven experience operating multiple types of heavy equipment, including backhoes, rollers, loaders, excavators, and others.


Good knowledge of equipment operation, maintenance, and safety practices.


Ability to interpret and follow project plans, drawings, and instructions.


Strong hand-eye coordination and depth perception.


Excellent spatial awareness and judgment of distances and angles.

Purpose






As the Supervisor, Registered Mine Electrician, you will lead site electrical safety, compliance, training and authorisation practices across the Lihir operation. 


Appointed by the Registered Mine Manager, this role is responsible for ensuring personnel who operate, work on, or work near electrical apparatus meet site requirements and statutory obligations. You will play a key role in maintaining the safety and integrity of the site electrical system, ensuring compliance with the Newmont Electrical Safety Management Plan, the High Voltage Safety Management Plan, Newmont site standards, and relevant Australian/New Zealand electrical standards. 


This role is suited to an experienced Electrical Engineer with strong electrical safety management experience, practical mine or heavy industry electrical knowledge, and the confidence to provide technical authority, guidance and assurance across site electrical activities.


 










Essential Duties








Maintain the safety and integrity of the site electrical system across the Lihir operation.


Ensure site electrical works comply with the Electrical Safety Management Plan and High Voltage Safety Management Plan.


Authorise amendments to the Electrical Safety Management Plan and ensure regular review and effectiveness checks are completed.


Authorise new electrical installations, alterations and personnel for licensed electrical work in line with site requirements.


Maintain site registers for licensed electricians, authorised persons, safety observers and licensed electrical contractors.


Review electrical licences and personnel qualifications to confirm authorisation requirements are met. 


Audit electrical workers to ensure they hold the correct competencies for the tasks they are completing. 


Review inspection and test records to ensure required testing is completed before approving Notifications of Energisation. 


Complete Certificates of Compliance and confirm installations meet AS/NZS 3000 and Newmont standards. 


Lead or support electrical safety incident investigations, identify actions and ensure outcomes are implemented and documented












Training & Experience








Electrical Engineering Degree.


Ability to obtain a PNG Power Authority Electrical Licence.


LVR/CPR certification.


Strong working knowledge of AS/NZS 3000 Wiring Rules.


Detailed understanding of AS/NZS 3007 Electrical installations for mines, AS/NZS 4871 Electrical equipment for mines and quarries, AS/NZS 3012 Construction electrical, and AS/NZS 60079 Hazardous Areas.


Strong knowledge of high voltage safety, HV switchgear and protection systems.


Experience working within electrical safety management systems, high voltage safety management plans and site electrical standards.


Experience authorising electrical personnel, reviewing electrical licences and maintaining compliance records.


Strong incident investigation skills, including the ability to identify actions and ensure they are implemented.


Ability to liaise across electrical, maintenance, engineering, operations and leadership teams to provide technical clarification and guidance.

28101.description:
About Lihir


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.

Summary






In this role, you will be responsible for overseeing the construction and maintenance of projects at various construction sites. You will collaborate with project managers, architects, subcontractors, and other stakeholders to ensure that projects are executed efficiently, safely, and within budget. Your expertise in technical principles, problem-solving, and attention to detail will be crucial in ensuring the successful completion of construction projects.


Duties and Responsibilities








Project Execution: Coordinate and manage the construction activities on-site, ensuring adherence to project plans, specifications, and timelines.


Quality Assurance: Conduct regular inspections to ensure construction work meets quality standards and complies with relevant codes, regulations, and safety guidelines.


Resource Management: Plan and allocate resources effectively, including labor, equipment, and materials, to optimize productivity and minimize delays.


Technical Expertise: Provide technical guidance and support to construction teams, including interpretation of engineering drawings, resolving design issues, and recommending appropriate solutions.


Collaboration: Collaborate with project managers, architects, subcontractors, and other stakeholders to ensure smooth coordination and communication throughout the construction process.


Risk Management: Identify potential risks and challenges, develop mitigation strategies, and implement appropriate measures to minimize disruptions to project timelines and budget.


Documentation: Maintain accurate and up-to-date project documentation, including daily progress reports, material quantities, site instructions, and variations from initial plans.


Health and Safety: Promote and enforce strict adherence to health and safety policies and procedures to maintain a safe working environment for all personnel on-site.


Problem Solving: Identify and resolve construction-related issues and conflicts promptly, offering innovative solutions to ensure project progress and client satisfaction.


Client Relationship: Foster positive relationships with clients, addressing their concerns, providing regular project updates, and ensuring their satisfaction throughout the construction process.




Job Requirements








Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or a related field.


Proven experience working as a Site Engineer in construction projects.


Strong knowledge of engineering principles, construction techniques, and building codes.


Proficiency in reading and interpreting construction drawings, blueprints, and specifications.


Familiarity with construction management software and tools.


Excellent organizational and time management skills.


Strong communication and interpersonal abilities.


Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.


Attention to detail and problem-solving mindset.


Knowledge of health and safety regulations and practices.




Others




Physical Requirements:




Ability to perform physical tasks such as walking, climbing, bending, and lifting heavy objects as required on construction sites.


Excellent hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity for operating tools and equipment.


Good vision and hearing abilities to detect potential hazards and communicate effectively in a construction environment.


Physical fitness and stamina to work in various weather conditions and navigate large construction sites.

Willingness to travel and work on-site at different construction locations as per project requirements.

28530.description:
Join Islands Petroleum as our Payroll Accountant


Islands Petroleum is seeking an experienced and technically strong 
Payroll Accountant
 to take ownership of key accounting, reconciliation, taxation and control activities supporting our end-to-end payroll function.


This is not simply a payroll processing role. We are looking for an accounting professional who understands the financial disciplines behind payroll - someone who can reconcile payroll accounts, validate tax calculations, establish robust working templates, maintain audit schedules, investigate variances and strengthen payroll controls.


The successful candidate will help ensure that payroll is accurate, compliant, fully reconciled and audit-ready, while partnering closely with Human Resources and Finance to continuously improve payroll processes.


 


Key Responsibilities:




Managing and supporting the end-to-end payroll process, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time


Performing detailed payroll reconciliations, including reconciliation of payroll control accounts, deductions, benefits, taxes and other payroll-related balance sheet accounts.


Preparing, reviewing and validating employee income tax calculations, statutory deductions and other payroll taxation requirements.


Assisting with the preparation and submission of group tax reports, statutory returns and related payments.


Preparing payroll journals and working closely with Finance to ensure payroll costs and liabilities are correctly recorded in the general ledger.


Investigating payroll and accounting variances and ensuring reconciling items are appropriately supported, corrected and cleared.


Developing and maintaining standard payroll reconciliation templates, calculation workbooks, control checklists and supporting schedules to improve consistency and accuracy.


Establishing and maintaining comprehensive monthly, year-end and audit schedules with appropriate supporting documentation and clear audit trails.


Conducting routine internal payroll audits, identifying control weaknesses and implementing corrective and preventative actions.


Ensuring payroll transactions, employee records and supporting documentation are complete, accurate, securely maintained and readily available for audit.


Producing accurate payroll reports, reconciliations and financial information for management, HR and Finance.


Supporting continuous improvement initiatives aimed at improving payroll efficiency, financial controls, accuracy and productivity.


Providing technical guidance, coaching and support to junior payroll team members.




 


Technical & Accounting Requirements:


We are particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate strong capability in:


Payroll accounting and reconciliation;




Payroll control and balance sheet account reconciliations.


General ledger reconciliation and variance analysis.


Payroll preparation, balancing and internal controls.


Payroll journals, accruals and liability management.




Taxation and statutory compliance;




Payroll income tax calculations.


Preparation and reconciliation of payroll taxes and statutory deductions.


Tax reporting and payment processes.


Strong understanding of payroll compliance requirements.




Audit and financial controls;




Preparation of detailed audit schedules and supporting working papers.


Internal payroll auditing and control testing.


Investigation and resolution of discrepancies.


Maintaining clear, accurate and traceable supporting documentation




Systems and analytical capability;




Advanced proficiency in 
Microsoft Excel
, including the ability to develop structured reconciliation templates and analytical workbooks.


Experience using integrated payroll or ERP systems  


Knowledge of 
Pronto
 would be highly regarded.


Strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving capability.




 


Qualification & Experience:


To be successful in this role, you should have:




A Bachelor's degree in Accounting, or a related discipline such as Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Statistics or Actuarial Science.


At least 5 years' experience in payroll accounting, payroll administration or a closely related accounting role.


Experience supporting payroll in a large and complex organisation, preferably involving more than 1,000 employees.


Demonstrated experience performing payroll and account reconciliations.


Exposure to auditing, financial controls and compliance activities.


Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify and resolve complex payroll discrepancies.


The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with HR, Finance, management and external stakeholders.


High standards of integrity, confidentiality and professional accountability.




 


The Candidate We Are Looking For:


You are likely to be an accountant who has developed strong payroll expertise, rather than someone whose experience has been limited to transactional payroll processing.


You will be comfortable moving between payroll calculations, Excel workbooks, reconciliations, tax calculations, general ledger accounts, audit schedules and payroll systems. Most importantly, you will have the discipline to ensure that every payroll cycle can be properly reconciled, explained and supported.


If you have a strong accounting foundation, enjoy solving reconciliation issues and want the opportunity to strengthen payroll controls and processes across a large organisation, we would like to hear from you.


 


What are the benefits for working with Islands Petroleum?




Opportunity to work with a market leader within the Petroleum sector in PNG.


Be part of a diverse, dynamic, cross-cultural setting, contributing significantly to our company's success.


Join a company that values its employees and recognizes their contribution.


Competitive remuneration and employee benefits 


Opportunities for career growth, learning, and development 


A culture built on teamwork, integrity, and accountability 


The opportunity to make meaningful contributions to the business and community. 




 


At Islands Petroleum, we don't just offer jobs, we provide opportunities to build rewarding careers and be part of a team that drives success together.

ASSISTANT PROJECT OFFICER - MANUS PROVINCE PROGRAMME


 


Organization Background


The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-government organization committed to working with communities, government and other partners to manage wildlife, lands and seas for biodiversity and human well-being. WCS PNG seeks an 
Assistant Project Officer 
to be based In Lorengau, Manus Province. The position will report to the Manus Community Engagement Officer. *
Experienced Manus-based candidates are encouraged to apply.


 


Role Dimension


This position will support field activities pertaining to community-based marine and terrestrial environmental management, ecological and socioeconomic monitoring, livelihood activities, and conservation in support for WCS’s programme of work on watershed management and community-driven spatial marine and terrestrial conservation areas. as directed by the supervisor. Accordingly, activities may relate to logistics, planning, acquittals, community engagement through the free, prior and informed consent (FPIC) process, data collection, education and awareness and other WCS activities.


 


Key Selection Criteria


Qualifications and requirements




Ideally with a bachelor’s degree, in science or relevant discipline (marine or natural sciences or natural resource management), or an equivalent qualification. Candidates with other qualifications with demonstrated interest or experience in marine conservation issues will also be considered.




Experience




Experience in community engagement, the free, prior and informed consent (FPIC) process, data collection, entry and analysis, and report writing.


Good understanding of environmental management, and the social, cultural and economic issues related to marine and terrestrial land protected areas.


Good interpersonal skills and experience in liaising with a range of stakeholders, including communities and landowners, local and state governments, the private sector, special interest groups and individuals about natural resource management issues.


Exposure to non-profit sectors (such as NGO or international organisations) is an advantage.


Fluency in written and spoken Tok Pisin and English.




 


Critical Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities




Excellent computer literacy and working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications (including Excel, Word, PowerPoint).


Good analytical and problem-solving skills.


Strong communication and engaging social-awareness skills


Being a self-starter with drive, initiative and able to work as both a team and individual with a positive attitude and an open mind.
